page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Daldv6 family. It is equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The physical hardware configuration consists of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, which yields a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 945 GB disk, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scoring in the top 25%. Text processing is also highly efficient, ranking in the top 10% of Geekbench tests. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls within the average range. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block reads and large-block writes perform at average levels, uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC processor, this server provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of a 945 GB local storage disk makes it suitable for applications requiring fast local scratch space. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded applications, text processing pipelines, software compilation, and light-to-medium database operations.
